key_insight: Medical multimodal LLMs can sound confident even when wrong, and this paper shows calibration can be substantially improved with a fusion-based interrogation plus expert-LMM assessment approach.
clinical_relevance: Better confidence calibration in medical VQA could make AI-assisted diagnosis and triage more trustworthy by reducing overconfident errors and better surfacing correct answers.
method: Uses Multi-Strategy Fusion-Based Interrogation (MS-FBI) to probe model responses from multiple angles.
Adds auxiliary expert LLM assessment to refine confidence estimation.
Focuses on aligning predicted confidence with actual answer accuracy in medical VQA.
evidence_signal: Across three medical VQA datasets, the proposed method reduced Expected Calibration Error (ECE) by an average of 40%, indicating markedly better confidence–accuracy alignment.
watch_item: Improved calibration does not guarantee clinical correctness or safety in real-world settings, so external validation and workflow safeguards are still needed.
paper_title: Confidence Calibration for Multimodal LLMs: An Empirical Study through Medical VQA
